fixtures.name: 1,3,5-tris(alkylidene)cyclohexane, propylidene against two ethylidene
fixtures.source: found by comparing generated ring molecules with RDKit, not by a public name (issue #120). The two ring branches at the propylidene carbon tie under Rules 1a to 2 and Rule 3 separates them by the descriptors of the two ethylidene bonds, E and Z here. The model ranks the ends of a ligand double bond in the whole molecule, where the propylidene bond and its far end are part of what the ranking looks at; RDKit 2022.03.2 ranks them inside the digraph rooted at the propylidene carbon, where they are not, and labels the bond Z (the whole-molecule reading gives E). Which reading IUPAC intends is not settled, so the propylidene bond is refused; the two ethylidene bonds do not depend on it and agree

fixtures.name: acyclic bond whose two ligands hold a double bond ranked through the bond
fixtures.source: each ligand is CH2-C(isobutyl)=CH-CH3. At the double bond inside a ligand, the two substituents (the CH2 that leads back to the labeled bond, and the isobutyl) tie at the first two spheres and are separated by what lies beyond the labeled bond's own atom: the model counts that atom's double-bond partner as a substituent, RDKit's digraph (rooted at that atom, partner left out) does not, and the two give opposite descriptors for the inner bonds and so opposite labels for the labeled bond (RDKit E). Refused; the inner bonds do not depend on it and agree

fixtures.name: the same bond with ethyl in place of isobutyl
fixtures.source: the inner bonds are separated at the first sphere whichever way the labeled bond is seen, so the descriptor is the same in both readings and the model labels the bond (RDKit agrees)

fixtures.name: the same bond with equal inner descriptors
fixtures.source: both ligands read E in both readings, so they tie and the bond is not stereogenic (RDKit agrees)

fixtures.name: acyclic bond whose two ligands are rings with an exocyclic double bond
fixtures.source: found by comparing generated molecules with RDKit. The two ligands are the same ring with the exocyclic double bond on opposite sides; the model ranks the ends of that ring bond in the whole molecule, where its ring closes on itself, and RDKit's digraph closes it at the atom where the ring was entered, so the two readings can rank its ring neighbors differently. RDKit labels the bond E (the whole-molecule reading gives Z). A descriptor ranked through a closed ring is refused; the ring bonds themselves agree

fixtures.name: center whose ligands hold a ring with an exocyclic double bond
fixtures.source: found by comparing generated ring molecules with RDKit. Atom 0 is separated from its ring neighbor only by Rule 3 on the ring double bonds, ranked through the ring that closes on itself; RDKit labels it S where the whole-molecule reading gives R (the same difference as above, here for a center). Refused; the other two centers do not need it and agree

fixtures.name: tetramethylenecyclobutane

fixtures.name: 1,3-diethylidene-2,4-dimethylenecyclobutane
fixtures.source: the ring end of each ethylidene bond ties between its two ring neighbors, and the =CH2 bonds tie at their =CH2 end, so Rule 3 only meets bonds that are not stereogenic in either reading (RDKit agrees)

fixtures.name: 1,2,3,4-tetra(alkylidene)cyclobutane, propylidene and three ethylidene
fixtures.source: found by comparing generated ring molecules with RDKit. The cyclobutane closes on itself within the ranking of an ethylidene bond's ring end, so the descriptors of the two ethylidene bonds next to the propylidene bond are refused, and with them the propylidene bond and the ethylidene bond opposite it. The two bonds that remain are labeled as RDKit does

fixtures.name: =CH2 on a carbon whose two equal arms hold double bonds that read differently from inside
fixtures.source: each arm is CH2-C(isobutyl)=CH-CH3 with an E bond, so the two arms tie by Rule 3 and the labeled bond is read through their descriptors, which the labeled bond's own atoms change (see the fixture before this one). The =CH2 end ties on its two hydrogens without reading anything, so the bond is not stereogenic in any reading and is `none` (RDKit agrees); the same arms beside a =CH-CH3 end are refused. The inner bonds do not depend on it and agree

fixtures.name: center with two tied ligands that hold propenyl groups, three spheres of twins
fixtures.source: the two ligands are equal in every respect, so the center is not stereogenic (RDKit agrees). Each quaternary carbon of a ligand asks whether two of its positions could differ, and the answer needs the descriptors of the propenyl bonds below it; the work of a descriptor is counted once for all of those questions (see cip.rs)

fixtures.name: two fused four-membered rings with ring double bonds, center at the fusion (issue #123)
fixtures.source: found by comparing generated small-ring molecules with RDKit 2022.03.2 (issue #123). Rules 1a and 2 leave the order of two ligands to Rule 1b, which compares the duplicate that a double bond adds to the far atom (of its parent, nearer the root) with a duplicate of the far end in the same sphere. The rule's text measures a duplicate to 'the corresponding nonduplicated atom' and does not say which is meant; RDKit ranks both in their own sphere and labels the atom S. This model's literal reading and RDKit's order the ligands differently here, so the center is refused, not labeled
fixtures.rdkit_differs: RDKit labels the atom S; the two readings of Rule 1b can order the ligands differently, which the model does not choose between
